QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_32

question.text: Ms. Sunita Patil (SIA) is debating whether to issue 'limited assurance' or 'reasonable assurance' on Bal Vikas Samiti's outcome metrics. Which statement correctly distinguishes the two?

answer.text: Reasonable assurance provides a higher level of confidence and requires more extensive procedures, expressed positively ('in our opinion, the outcomes are fairly presented'); limited assurance provides a lower level, expressed negatively ('nothing has come to our attention that would cause us to believe…')
Limited assurance is higher; reasonable assurance is lower
Both provide identical levels of confidence
Limited assurance is only used for Big Four firms; reasonable for others

explanation.text: The Logic: Reasonable assurance provides a higher level of confidence and requires more extensive evidence-gathering procedures, expressed in positive form ('in our opinion the outcomes are fairly presented in all material respects'). Limited assurance provides a lower level of confidence, uses less extensive procedures, and is expressed in negative form ('nothing has come to our attention that would cause us to believe…'). This is the standard international assurance-framework convention. The Trap: Options B and C reverse or flatten the levels and are factually wrong. Option D invents a firm-type rule that does not exist; assurance levels are not tied to firm category. Note: The reasonable-versus-limited assurance distinction is not defined in the cited Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook (January 2026) pages 124-125, 138 or 200. Pages 138 and 200 state that the SIA report should not be construed as assurance, and page 138 instead describes unqualified/unmodified and qualified/modified opinions. The framing above reflects general assurance-framework knowledge (e.g., ISAE 3000).
